req.title: Reuse db connection per request
req.statement: The system shall reuse a single sqlite3 connection per Flask request via flask.g.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-025 requires that a single sqlite3 connection is reused per Flask request via flask.g. The key behaviors to test are: (1) positive — get_db() called twice within the same app context returns the identical connection object; (2) negative — get_db() called in separate request contexts returns distinct connection objects (no cross-request leakage); (3) boundary — after a request context tears down, g.db is removed (close_db clears it), so a fresh context starts with no cached connection. Additional tests cover that the connection is a real sqlite3.Connection, that row_factory is set to sqlite3.Row, and that the HTTP endpoint still returns 200 while the connection reuse invariant holds.

tests.name: test_get_db_returns_same_object_within_single_request_context
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp DATABASE path
actions: Push a single app context
Call get_db() twice within that context
Compare the two returned objects with 'is'
expected: Both calls return the exact same sqlite3.Connection instance (identity check)
trace: R-FLASKR-025: single connection per request reused via flask.g
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os, sqlite3
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

def test_get_db_returns_same_object_within_single_request_context():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
        conn1 = get_db()
        conn2 = get_db()
        assert conn1 is conn2, "get_db() must return the same connection object within one context"
        assert conn1.row_factory is sqlite3.Row, "row_factory must be sqlite3.Row"
    os.unlink(path)

test_get_db_returns_same_object_within_single_request_context()

tests.name: test_get_db_returns_different_objects_across_separate_request_contexts
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp DATABASE path
actions: Push first app context, call get_db(), record id, pop context
Push second app context, call get_db(), record id, pop context
Compare the two connection ids
expected: The two connection objects are NOT the same instance (different ids)
Each context produces its own fresh connection
trace: R-FLASKR-025: connection must NOT leak across request boundaries
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

def test_get_db_returns_different_objects_across_separate_request_contexts():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    with app.app_context():
        conn1 = get_db()
        id1 = id(conn1)
    with app.app_context():
        conn2 = get_db()
        id2 = id(conn2)
    assert id1 != id2, "Separate request contexts must produce distinct connection objects"
    os.unlink(path)

test_get_db_returns_different_objects_across_separate_request_contexts()

tests.name: test_close_db_removes_connection_from_g_at_context_teardown
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp DATABASE path
actions: Push app context, call get_db() to populate g.db
Manually call close_db() to simulate teardown
Check that g no longer has 'db' attribute
Call get_db() again and verify a new connection is created
expected: After close_db(), 'db' is absent from flask.g
Subsequent get_db() call creates a new connection (not None)
trace: R-FLASKR-025: boundary — connection lifecycle ends exactly at teardown
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flask import g
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, close_db, init_db

def test_close_db_removes_connection_from_g_at_context_teardown():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
        conn = get_db()
        assert 'db' in g.__dict__ or hasattr(g, 'db'), "g.db must exist after get_db()"
        close_db()
        assert g.get('db') is None, "g.db must be absent after close_db()"
        conn2 = get_db()
        assert conn2 is not None, "get_db() after close_db() must return a new connection"
    os.unlink(path)

test_close_db_removes_connection_from_g_at_context_teardown()

tests.name: test_http_request_reuses_single_db_connection_and_returns_200
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp DATABASE path
Database initialised with init_db() (pre-loaded rows present)
actions: Use app.test_client() to GET /
Assert HTTP 200 response
Within a separate app context, call get_db() twice and assert identity
expected: Within one app context get_db() is idempotent (same object)
trace: R-FLASKR-025: HTTP request completes successfully while connection reuse holds
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os, sqlite3
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

def test_http_request_reuses_single_db_connection_and_returns_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    with app.app_context():
        c1 = get_db()
        c2 = get_db()
        assert c1 is c2
        assert isinstance(c1, sqlite3.Connection)
    os.unlink(path)

test_http_request_reuses_single_db_connection_and_returns_200()

Call get_db()
Assert type is sqlite3.Connection

import tempfile, os, sqlite3
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

def test_get_db_connection_is_sqlite3_connection_with_correct_row_factory():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

tests.name: test_get_db_called_zero_times_means_no_db_in_g
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp DATABASE path
Fresh app context pushed but get_db() never called
actions: Push app context without calling get_db()
Check that flask.g does not have 'db' key
expected: g.get('db') returns None when get_db() has not been called
trace: R-FLASKR-025: boundary — connection only created on first call, not before
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flask import g
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_get_db_called_zero_times_means_no_db_in_g():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    with app.app_context():
        result = g.get('db', None)
        assert result is None, "g.db must not exist before get_db() is called"
    os.unlink(path)

preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp DATABASE path
actions: Push app context
Call get_db() three times
Assert all three return values are the identical object
expected: All three calls return the same sqlite3.Connection instance
No new connection is created on the second or third call

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

def test_get_db_called_three_times_still_returns_same_object():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
        c1 = get_db()
        c2 = get_db()
        c3 = get_db()
        assert c1 is c2, "2nd call must return same object as 1st"
        assert c2 is c3, "3rd call must return same object as 2nd"
        assert id(c1) == id(c2) == id(c3), "all ids must be identical"
    os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_db_not_in_g_after_request_context_exits_via_teardown
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp DATABASE path
actions: Use test_client() to make a GET / request (triggers full request lifecycle)
After request completes, push a fresh app context
Verify g.get('db') is None in the new context (no leaked connection)
expected: After request teardown, a new context has no pre-existing g.db
trace: R-FLASKR-025: state transition — connection absent after request teardown
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flask import g
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_db_not_in_g_after_request_context_exits_via_teardown():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    with app.app_context():
        leaked = g.get('db', None)
        assert leaked is None, "g.db must not leak into a new context after request teardown"
    os.unlink(path)

test_db_not_in_g_after_request_context_exits_via_teardown()
